assessment: Close the remaining ACC tiled runtime gap with scalar weighted SW albedo mapping
scope: NVHPC 24.5, SP RRTMG/McICA, A100-SXM4-40GB; same 16960-column/137-level workload, NPROMA=32, K=32, two GPU ranks. SP/DP correctness checks use the smaller controlled and wide inputs.
changes: ACC weighted SW albedo mapping reuses the existing explicit-shape scalar get_albedo_bands_omp helper, with ACC gang/vector parallelism and sequential native-band accumulation. Retain the helper name and public interface.
Keep the original ACC zero-weight skip and OMP accumulation policy; preserve separate direct/diffuse albedos and copy diffuse to direct on the device when the direct input is absent.
Remove the unused ACC sw_albedo_band/lw_albedo_band device mappings. Native CPU weighted mappings still use their existing host scratch arrays and arithmetic.
Retain the bounded driver staging, source-release-before-physics lifetime and existing gather/scatter implementation.

protocol.statistic: Five alternating-order process groups, six iterations per process, first iteration excluded; median of the five group medians. Timed GPU iteration is the maximum of two rank times.
protocol.timing: Synchronized full radiation iterations, including iteration transfers and gather/scatter, excluding initialization and NetCDF I/O. All reported new timing ratios are paired within an allocation.
protocol.memory: MiB; maximum across groups of the sum of process peak RSS or 20-ms-sampled NVML device peaks. Includes CUDA context/reservations; rank peaks are not necessarily simultaneous.
protocol.reference_ownership_clarification: The tiled fork creates resident zrgp storage outside the timer, but updates input fields inside every timed iteration. The integration uses bounded per-tile source mappings. Residency alone does not isolate the remaining overhead.
protocol.omp_timing_control: Unchanged integrated OMP implementation built at the preceding checkpoint; the shared helper's OMP loop and arithmetic are unchanged. The current SP/DP OMP source also rebuilds successfully.

target_assessment.interpretation: The remaining strict ACC tiled target is met in both new allocations, with a narrow approximately 0.4 percentage-point margin. CPU and other valid-base runtime/memory assessments remain recorded in the preceding report; they were not all rebenchmarked here.

profiling.interpretation: One older kernel becomes two explicit scalar-helper calls (direct and diffuse). Approximately 87.1 us becomes 9.0 us per radiation call, or about 0.70 ms saved across nine tiles per rank/iteration. Profiles cover complete processes and are separate from unprofiled acceptance timings; this is diagnostic evidence, not a paired before/after whole-iteration speedup measurement.

saved_output_equivalence.scope: All saved numerical variables in active columns; inactive offset-driver output is unspecified and excluded.

compute_sanitizer.scope: SP/DP standalone weighted mapping with non-unit active range

additional_cpu_sp_weighted_smoke.reference: Saved matched-sampling CPU correctness output, built with a different flag configuration

validation.quick_check: One S1 END IF style finding; the spelling follows radiation/CONVENTIONS. No other added-line findings.
validation.fortls: Attempted on the changed source; launcher exits 1 without diagnostics.

limitations: The existing larger-input GPU/matched-CPU LW difference remains 0.003814697265625 W/m2, exceeding the unchanged 0.001 threshold. The valid GPU references share it. No full-domain CPU/GPU correctness claim is made.
Performance remains specific to the measured SP workload, tile width and hardware. The preceding report's solver, scaling and interface coverage limits still apply.
The diffuse-only fallback is preserved in the implementation; no separate new end-to-end absent-direct-input case was added.
